pairings.thesis: Stretch. A material exit is an event you hold through; the put may be cheap relative to the downside. High-JEV first announcements vs low-JEV recasts (KO June filing).

Written before any P&L. P-leadership-low pooled leadership 8-Ks without asking whether the news was new. An 8-K must be filed within four business days, so many leadership excerpts report a change announced days or weeks earlier whose news the options market has already priced. Fresh filings (announcement written in the excerpt at most 1 session before the first tradeable close) are the ones where post-filing premium still carries news uncertainty that overstates the move that follows. Prediction: selling the 5% OTM put at the filing-session close earns more than on ordinary days (fresh vs placebo > 0), more than on stale filings (fresh - stale > 0), and the edge falls with lag (lag 0 and 1 above lag 4+). A null on fresh vs placebo, or an edge that does not fall with lag, rejects it.
pairings.notes: In-sample (freeze-v2, EDGAR period-of-report dates): fresh n=55 edge=-1.19% (IN-SAMPLE ONLY worse), stale n=95 edge=-0.16% (NOT SUPPORTED), fresh-stale=-1.03% (NOT SUPPORTED - fresh WORSE). Lag buckets: lag0=-1.78%, lag1=-0.93%, lag2=+0.40%, lag3=-0.79%, lag4+=-0.18%. No monotonic decay with lag. Audit: all 10 checked events have correct fresh/stale classification per period-of-report date. Top performers mostly stale (PLTR, UNH, INTC, NFLX); bottom performers mostly fresh (BA, CRM, UNH). Hypothesis rejected in-sample: fresh filings do not over-price the move. EDGAR period-of-report may be earlier than public announcement, mixing arms. Null result reported as finding.
